nl.statement: A real-outcome observational experiment with a finite discrete confounder. One full-data unit is \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) with \(X\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(A\in\{0,1\}\) and real potential outcomes; the law \(P\) is determined by the cell masses \(p_k=P(X=k)\), the propensities \(\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k)\), and the arm-and-cell conditional outcome laws on \(\mathbb R\). Consistency \(Y=Y(A)\) and conditional exchangeability \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X\) hold, treatment satisfies fixed strong overlap \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass cell, and the outcome is controlled only through \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M/2\) and \(E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le M^2\); no boundedness of \(Y\) is assumed. The observed record is \(O=(X,A,Y)\) with law \(P_O\), and the sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) is drawn from \(Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}\), with the same product construction at block size \(m\). — Search trace: read `grep '^## ' ../doc/API.md` section index and §8h `PO/`, §12 `Stat/`, §13sa `Estimation/MinimaxATE/`, §10z reusable minimax substrate; then `Glob CausalSmith/Stat/**/*.lean` and `lean_file_outline` on `CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap_Research/Basic.lean`. Result: the closest world is `CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap.DiscreteLaw` / `Obs d` (see S2), but that world is a PMF on `Fin d x Bool x Bool` -- a BINARY outcome. The frozen core is stated for real outcomes controlled only by a conditional second central moment (`ass:second-central-moment`), so the binary world is a strictly different abstraction and cannot carry the class; `Causalean/PO/` supplies measure-theoretic PO systems over general outcome spaces but no finite-cell arbitrary-mass discrete-confounder law with per-cell arm outcome measures. Mathlib side checked with `lean_leansearch` ('expectation of one over binomial count plus one') -- only `PMF.binomial`/`PMF.bernoulli`, no packaged experiment. Hence `bypass-justified`: local record type carrying `p : Fin d -> R`, `pi : Fin d -> R`, and `nu : Bool -> Fin d -> Measure R`, with `productLaw` built by `Measure.pi`, reusing Causalean's `Stat.Sample` product plumbing. The full-data layer adds the joint potential-outcome law used by `ass:consistency` / `ass:conditional-exchangeability`.

The binary-outcome discrete-confounder experiment of Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han and Kennedy: one unit is \((X,A,B)\) with \(X\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and \(A,B\in\{0,1\}\), arbitrary cell masses, fixed overlap \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\), arm response means \(\eta_{ak}\in[0,1]\), and an \(n\)-fold product sampling law. This is the source experiment for the cited converse lemmas, and the affine map \(B(a)\mapsto M\{B(a)-1/2\}\) together with the Bernoulli contraction channel embeds it into the ambient world \(S1\). — Highest-leverage reuse decision in the plan. The banked sibling paper `stat_discrete_ate_minimax_loggap_polynomial_upper_match` already formalizes exactly this binary source world: `DiscreteLaw d`, `Obs d`, `Overlap`, `Consistency`, `ConditionalExchangeability`, `observedMarginal`, `ateFunctional`, `productLaw`, `mse`, `worstCaseMSE`, `minimaxRisk`, `oneArmMinimaxRisk`, `ControlZeroLaw`, and the cited-gate Prop `ZengOneArmMinimaxLower` (verified by `lean_file_outline` on Basic.lean and `Grep ZengOneArmMinimaxLower` in Helpers/LowerBound.lean). Every binary-source lemma of the present core is stated in this world, so the embedding lemmas (`prop:zeng-class-inclusion-and-lower-transfer`, `lem:scaled-binary-exact-lower-transfer-all-d`, `thm:radius-channel-converse-all-d`) are bridges from S2 to S1 rather than fresh constructions.

The law \(P\) carries an arm-cell outcome distribution for every arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and \emph{every} cell \(k\), zero-mass cells included; let \(\mu_{ak}\) denote its mean.  Whenever the arm-cell probability \(P(A=a,X=k)\) is positive, \(\mu_{ak}\) is the observed conditional mean \(E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]\).  Only supported cells are constrained: for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\),
\[
|\mu_{ak}|\le M/2 .
\]

review.note: Quantification over Bool covers exactly both treatment levels, and the positive-cell condition and bound |mu_ak| ≤ M/2 match verbatim.

For \emph{every} cell \(k\), let
\[
\tau_k:=\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}
\]
and
\[
\delta_k:=\tau_k-\sum_j p_j\tau_j ,
\]
both well defined on zero-mass cells as well.
The cell-effect deviations satisfy
\[
\max_{k:p_k>0}|\delta_k|\le \sigma M .
\]

review.note: For the finite supported-cell set, the universal bound is equivalent to the stated maximum bound, and cellDeviation unfolds to tau_k minus the weighted ATE sum.

Let
\[
O:=(X,A,Y)\in\mathcal O:=\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R,
\]
and let \(P_O\) denote the observed-data law of \(O\) under \(P\). The \(n\)-sample observed-data experiments generated by \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) are
\[
\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
:=
\left\{
Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}:P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
\right\}.
\]

review.note: Membership is exactly existence of a model-class law whose observed n-sample measure is its n-fold product law.

nl.frozen_body:
For a real-outcome finite-cell law \(P\) indexed by \(k=1,\ldots,d\) and an overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), assume consistency, conditional exchangeability of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) and \(A\) given \(X\) for measurable potential-outcome events, overlap \(\epsilon\le \pi_k\le 1-\epsilon\) whenever \(p_k>0\), and first-moment integrability of each arm-cell outcome law for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and positive-mass cell. With \(p_k\) the cell mass and \(\mu_{ak}\) the arm-cell conditional outcome mean, define
\[
\tau(P)
:=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}).
\]

review.note: On the stated causal-identification domain, the definition is exactly the weighted finite-cell formula, while ate_identification supplies its equality to the full-data causal expectation.

nl.statement: Split the observations into two independent blocks \(I_0\) and \(I_1\).  The block \(I_0\) is used only to classify cells as heavy or light by empirical occupancy.  On light cells, use fixed shifted-Chebyshev coefficients of degree proportional to \(\log(en)\), evaluated on \(I_1\) by ordered distinct-index falling-factorial statistics carrying exactly one normalized outcome mark.  On heavy cells, use indicator-totalized arm sample-mean differences on \(I_1\), weighted by the \(I_1\) empirical cell frequency.  Sum the light and heavy contributions, multiply by \(M\), and clip to \([-M,M]\).  Set the estimator to zero outside the calibrated range.  The constants, degree, occupancy threshold, positive-denominator indicators, and fallbacks are those in Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:continuous\text{-}ratio\text{-}polynomial\text{-}upper}\).
nl.frozen_body:
For observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), with \(X_i\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(A_i\in\{0,1\}\), and \(Y_i\in\mathbb R\), fix a polynomial handle \((N,\rho)\) with \(\rho>0\).  Let \(L:=\log(en)\),
\[
D_6:=8\log(27/4),
\qquad
\alpha_0:=\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{64\log 6},\frac{1}{512D_6}\right\},
\qquad
K_n:=\left\lfloor \alpha_0 L\right\rfloor .
\]
The handle certifies that \(2\le K_n\) whenever \(0<n\), \(0<d\), \(N\le n\), and \(d\le \rho nL\).  The active branch below is used on \(N\le n\) and \(d\le \rho nL\); the calibrated value is \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}=0\) when \(N>n\) or \(d>\rho nL\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item Split the sample into the pilot and estimation blocks
\[
I_0:=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},
\qquad
I_1:=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},
\qquad
m_1:=|I_1|=n-\lfloor n/2\rfloor .
\]

\item Use \(I_0\) to form the empirically heavy and light cell sets
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}
:=
\left\{k:256L<\sum_{i\in I_0}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\}\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}
:=
\{1,\ldots,d\}\setminus \widehat{\mathcal H}.
\]

\item On each heavy cell \(k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}\), use \(I_1\) to compute the estimation-block arm counts, cell count, arm outcome totals, totalized arm means, and normalized plug-in contribution
\[
N_{ak}^{(1)}
:=
\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\},
\qquad
N_k^{(1)}
:=
\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\},
\]
\[
S_{ak}^{(1)}
:=
\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i,
\qquad
\overline Y_{ak}^{(1)}
:=
\begin{cases}
S_{ak}^{(1)}/N_{ak}^{(1)}, & N_{ak}^{(1)}>0,\\
0, & N_{ak}^{(1)}=0,
\end{cases}
\]
\[
\widehat h_k
:=
\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}\,
\frac{\overline Y_{1k}^{(1)}-\overline Y_{0k}^{(1)}}{M}.
\]

\item On each light cell \(k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}\), set
\[
B:=\frac{4096L}{m_1},
\qquad
g_{K_n,j}:=
(-1)^j\frac{2^{2j+3}}{K_n(K_n+j+2)}{K_n+j+2\choose 2j+4},
\qquad
j=0,\ldots,K_n-2.
\]
With \((m)_r\) denoting the falling factorial, evaluate the ordered distinct-index one-mark statistic
\[
U_{k,a,j}
:=
\frac{1}{(m_1)_{j+2}}
\sum_{\substack{(i_0,\ldots,i_{j+1})\in I_1^{j+2}\\
i_0,\ldots,i_{j+1}\ \mathrm{distinct}}}
\frac{Y_{i_0}}{M}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_{i_0}=k,A_{i_0}=a\}
\left(\prod_{\ell=1}^{j}\mathbf 1\{X_{i_\ell}=k,A_{i_\ell}=a\}\right)
\mathbf 1\{X_{i_{j+1}}=k\},
\]
and set the normalized light-cell contribution to
\[
\widehat P_k
:=
\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}(-1)^{1-a}
\sum_{j=0}^{K_n-2}\frac{g_{K_n,j}}{B^{j+1}}U_{k,a,j}.
\]

\item Writing \(\operatorname{clip}_{[a,b]}(x):=\min\{b,\max\{a,x\}\}\) for truncation to the interval \([a,b]\), sum the heavy and light contributions and output the clipped active-branch statistic
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}
:=
M\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}
\left(
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}\widehat h_k
+
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\widehat P_k
\right).
\]
\end{enumerate}

review.note: After unfolding the raw program and its helpers, Lean implements the deterministic pilot/estimation split, pilot-only heavy/light classification, fixed shifted-Chebyshev one-mark factorial terms, estimation-block weighted arm means, calibrated active range, zero fallback, and M-scaled clipping stated in the note.

nl.statement:
From \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), let \(N_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\), \(N_k:=N_{0k}+N_{1k}\), \(S_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i\), \(I_k:=\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}N_{1k}>0\}\), and \(R_n:=\sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k\).  Put \(\overline Y_{ak}:=S_{ak}/N_{ak}\) when \(N_{ak}>0\), and define
\[
 T_n^{\mathrm{col}}:=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}\!\left(
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}
 \sum_{k=1}^dN_kI_k(\overline Y_{1k}-\overline Y_{0k})
 \right),
\]
with the inner value defined to be zero when \(R_n=0\).  The map is total, measurable, and computable by one pass through the sample followed by one pass through the occupied categories.
nl.frozen_body:
For observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), define \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) by the following one-pass cell aggregation followed by one pass through the occupied categories.

\begin{enumerate}
\item For each arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and cell \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), define the full-sample arm-cell count and outcome total
\[
N_{ak}
:=
\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\},
\qquad
S_{ak}
:=
\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i.
\]

\item Define the full-sample cell count, crossed-cell indicator, and total count in empirically crossed cells
\[
N_k:=N_{0k}+N_{1k},
\qquad
I_k:=\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}N_{1k}>0\},
\qquad
R_n:=\sum_{k=1}^d N_k I_k.
\]

\item For positive arm-cell counts, define the arm-cell sample means
\[
\overline Y_{ak}:=\frac{S_{ak}}{N_{ak}}
\qquad\text{when }N_{ak}>0.
\]

\item Output the occupancy-weighted treated-control statistic
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{col}}
:=
\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}
\left(
\frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}
\sum_{k=1}^d
N_kI_k(\overline Y_{1k}-\overline Y_{0k})
\right),
\]
where the inner value is \(0\) when \(R_n=0\).
\end{enumerate}

review.note: Unfolding usableTotal, usableCell, counts, sums, and empiricalArmMean gives exactly R_n, I_k, the indicator-totalized arm means, the R_n=0 fallback, and clipping in the displayed estimator.

nl.statement: For \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\), let \(u_{n,d}:=d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\), \(h_{n,d,\sigma}:=\sigma^2+d/n^2\), and define \[\widehat\tau_n^{\star}:=\begin{cases}T_n^{\mathrm{col}},&h_{n,d,\sigma}\le\min\{1,u_{n,d}\},\\T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},&u_{n,d}<\min\{1,h_{n,d,\sigma}\},\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] The displayed tie rule makes the selector a total measurable map for every \((n,d,\sigma)\).
nl.frozen_body:
Given candidate estimators \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) and \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\), each a total measurable map \(\mathcal O^n\to[-M,M]\), define \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\) by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the rare-cell polynomial remainder
\[
u_{n,d}:=\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}.
\]
\item Define the collision remainder
\[
h_{n,d,\sigma}:=\sigma^2+\frac{d}{n^2}.
\]
\item Output the measurable selector
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\star}:=
\begin{cases}
T_n^{\mathrm{col}},&h_{n,d,\sigma}\le\min\{1,u_{n,d}\},\\
T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},&u_{n,d}<\min\{1,h_{n,d,\sigma}\},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}

review.note: The unfolded polynomialComponent and collisionComponent are u_{n,d} and h_{n,d,sigma}, and the ordered Lean conditionals implement exactly the collision, polynomial, and zero branches with the stated tie rule.

nl.statement:
Let \(\lambda:=\sigma/2\).  Start from a fixed-sample binary one-arm hard family with at most \(d_{\mathrm{rad}}:=\min\{d,\max(1,\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}n\log(en)\rfloor)\}\) positive-mass cells, assign zero mass to unused cells, and pass each binary potential response through the hypothesis-independent kernel
\[
 B(a)\longmapsto B'(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left\{\frac12+\lambda\left(B(a)-\frac12\right)\right\},
 \qquad Y(a):=M\{B'(a)-1/2\}.
\]
For the exact-homogeneity component, scale a uniform-mass binary hard family on at most \(d_{\mathrm{ex}}:=\min\{d,\max(1,\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}n^2\rfloor)\}\) positive-mass cells by \(B(a)\mapsto M\{B(a)-1/2\}\), again assigning zero mass to unused cells.  Here \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}},b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}>0\) are fixed constants depending only on \(\epsilon\).  This construction handle names only the two embedded families and the channel; class membership, target separation, data processing, finite-sample cutoffs, and the resulting capped all-alphabet risk bounds are proved separately.
nl.frozen_body:
For fixed constants \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}},b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}>0\) depending only on \(\epsilon\), define the two embedded hard families and the channel as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Set the channel attenuation
\[
\lambda:=\frac{\sigma}{2}.
\]
\item For the radius component, set the capped alphabet size
\[
d_{\mathrm{rad}}:=\min\{d,\max(1,\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}n\log(en)\rfloor)\}.
\]
Start from a fixed-sample binary one-arm hard family with at most \(d_{\mathrm{rad}}\) positive-mass cells, and assign zero mass to unused cells.
\item Pass each binary potential response through the hypothesis-independent channel
\[
B'(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left\{\frac12+\lambda\left(B(a)-\frac12\right)\right\},
\]
and define the scaled real potential response
\[
Y(a):=M\{B'(a)-1/2\}.
\]
\item For the exact-homogeneity component, set the capped alphabet size
\[
d_{\mathrm{ex}}:=\min\{d,\max(1,\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}n^2\rfloor)\}.
\]
Start from a uniform-mass binary hard family on at most \(d_{\mathrm{ex}}\) positive-mass cells, assign zero mass to unused cells, and define
\[
Y(a):=M\{B(a)-1/2\}.
\]
\item The construction outputs the radius-channel embedded family, the exact-homogeneity embedded family, and the channel above.
\end{enumerate}

nl.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), the causal average treatment effect is identified from \(P_O\) by \(\tau(P)=\sum_{k=1}^{d}p_k\{E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=k]-E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]\}\).
nl.frozen_body:
For every dimension \(d\), overlap parameter \(\epsilon\), envelope level \(M\), radius \(\sigma\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, the average treatment effect functional \(\tau(P)\) of \cref{obj:def:ate-functional} equals the full-data causal contrast and is identified from the observed margin by the finite-cell g-formula:
\[
\tau(P)
=
\int \{Y(1)-Y(0)\}\,dP
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d} p_k
\left\{
E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=k]-E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]
\right\}.
\]

review.note: Unfolding causalATE, ateFunctional, rawAteFormula, and cellEffect gives exactly the causal expectation equal to the finite sum of cell masses times treated-minus-control conditional means; ModelClass supplies the paper's stated domain, and the RealLaw factorization pins every supported-cell mean to the observed margin.

nl.statement: Every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) satisfies \(|\tau_k|\le M\), \(|\tau(P)|\le M\), and \(\max_{k:p_k>0}|\delta_k|\le2M\). Consequently \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}=\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\).
nl.frozen_body:
For any \(d\in\mathbb N\) and any \(\epsilon,M\in\mathbb R\), let \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) be the model classes in \cref{obj:def:unrestricted-class,obj:def:model-class}. For each law \(P\), write
\[
\tau_k(P)=\mu_{1k}(P)-\mu_{0k}(P),
\qquad
\tau(P)=\sum_{k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}} p_k(P)\tau_k(P),
\qquad
\delta_k(P)=\tau_k(P)-\tau(P).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) satisfies
\[
|\tau_k(P)|\le M\quad\text{for every }k\text{ with }p_k(P)>0,
\qquad
|\tau(P)|\le M,
\]
and
\[
|\delta_k(P)|\le 2M\quad\text{for every }k\text{ with }p_k(P)>0.
\]
Consequently the two classes have the same underlying laws at radius \(2\): for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) there exists \(Q\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\) with the same law as \(P\), and for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\) there exists \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) with the same law as \(Q\).

Put \(L:=\log(en)\), \(b:=n^{-1}+d/n^2\), \(u:=d^2/(n^2L^2)\), and \(s:=\sigma^2\).  In the nonsaturated triangular regime \(L^2<d<nL\), the normalized selector and converse benchmarks
\[
 q:=\frac1n+\min\left\{u,s+\frac d{n^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 \ell:=b+su
\]
satisfy
\[
 \frac12\{b+\min(u,s)\}\le q\le b+\min(u,s),
 \qquad \ell=b+su.
\]
For every fixed \(\underline\sigma\in(0,2]\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}\le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(\underline\sigma\le\sigma\le2\) and \(1\le d\le c_{\epsilon}n^2/L\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
 \le \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
For every fixed \(C<\infty\), the same equivalence holds with constants independent of \(\sigma\in[0,2]\) whenever at least one of
\[
 u\ge1,
 \qquad u\le Cb,
 \qquad \sigma^2\le Cb
\]
holds.  The constant-free condition \(u\le b\) is exactly
\[
 d^2\le nL^2+dL^2.
\]
In particular, \(d\le\sqrt n\,L\) is sufficient, the former small-alphabet regime \(d\le L^2\) is retained, and matching holds for every admissible alphabet whenever \(\sigma^2\le C(n^{-1}+d/n^2)\).

Consequently, along a shrinking-radius sequence, the ratio of the current upper and lower benchmarks can diverge only in the residual wedge
\[
 b\ll u\ll1,
 \qquad
 b\ll\sigma^2\ll1.
\]
Up to boundary constants, this is \(\sqrt n\,L\ll d\ll nL\) together with \(\sigma^2\gg n^{-1}+d/n^2\).  The wedge is nonempty: for \(d_n=n\), \(L_n:=\log(en)\), and \(\sigma_n:=L_n^{-1/2}\), the selector benchmark divided by the proved lower benchmark satisfies
\[
 \frac{n^{-1}+\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2),\sigma_n^2+d_n/n^2\}}
 {n^{-1}+d_n/n^2+\sigma_n^2\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2)\}}
 \asymp L_n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus all endpoints, every fixed interior radius, saturation, the small-alphabet regime, and both parametric-dominance elbows are matched.  Only the displayed residual wedge can require a stronger constrained converse or a sharper estimator; neither endpoint-only reasoning nor the existing radius channel decides between them.

Put \(L:=\log(en)\), \(b:=n^{-1}+d/n^2\), \(u:=d^2/(n^2L^2)\), and \(s:=\sigma^2\).  In the nonsaturated triangular regime \(L^2<d<nL\), the normalized selector and converse benchmarks
\[
 q:=\frac1n+\min\left\{u,s+\frac d{n^2}\right\},
 \qquad
 \ell:=b+su
\]
satisfy
\[
 \frac12\{b+\min(u,s)\}\le q\le b+\min(u,s),
 \qquad \ell=b+su.
\]
For every fixed \(\underline\sigma\in(0,2]\), there are constants \(0<c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}\le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}<\infty\) such that, uniformly over \(\underline\sigma\le\sigma\le2\) and every integer \(d\ge1\),
\[
 c_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
 \le \mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
 \le C_{\epsilon,\underline\sigma}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
For every fixed \(C<\infty\), the same equivalence holds with constants independent of \(\sigma\in[0,2]\) whenever at least one of
\[
 u\ge1,
 \qquad u\le Cb,
 \qquad \sigma^2\le Cb
\]
holds.  The constant-free condition \(u\le b\) is exactly
\[
 d^2\le nL^2+dL^2.
\]
In particular, \(d\le\sqrt n\,L\) is sufficient, the regime \(d\le L^2\) is retained, and matching holds for every alphabet whenever \(\sigma^2\le C(n^{-1}+d/n^2)\).

Consequently, along a shrinking-radius sequence, the ratio of the all-alphabet upper and lower benchmarks can diverge only in the residual wedge
\[
 b\ll u\ll1,
 \qquad
 b\ll\sigma^2\ll1.
\]
Up to boundary constants, this is \(\sqrt n\,L\ll d\ll nL\) together with \(\sigma^2\gg n^{-1}+d/n^2\).  The wedge is nonempty: for \(d_n=n\), \(L_n:=\log(en)\), and \(\sigma_n:=L_n^{-1/2}\), the selector benchmark divided by the proved lower benchmark satisfies
\[
 \frac{n^{-1}+\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2),\sigma_n^2+d_n/n^2\}}
 {n^{-1}+\min(1,d_n/n^2)+\sigma_n^2\min\{1,d_n^2/(n^2L_n^2)\}}
 \asymp L_n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus both endpoints, every fixed interior radius, saturation, the small-alphabet regime, and both parametric-dominance elbows are matched for all alphabets.  Only the displayed residual wedge can require a stronger constrained converse or a sharper estimator; neither endpoint-only reasoning nor the existing radius channel decides between them.

\]

\[

\[
\left|
E_{P_n}[s]-\tau(P)
\right|
\le
\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}
+
2\exp\left\{-b_\epsilon\frac{n^2}{\max\{n,d\}}\right\}
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{P_n}(s)
\le
C_\epsilon\left(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}^2+\frac{d}{n^2}+\frac1n\right).
\]

Define
\[
u_{n,d}:=\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
h_{n,d,\sigma}:=\sigma^2+\frac{d}{n^2}.
\]
Then the published binary collision guarantee above and the following algebraic comparison hold simultaneously:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Pointwise comparison.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(\sigma\in\mathbb R\) such that \(n>0\), \(d>0\), and \(0\le \sigma\le 2\),
\[
\min\{1,\min\{u_{n,d},h_{n,d,\sigma}\}\}\le h_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Asymptotic comparison.)} For every pair of sequences \(d_n\in\mathbb N\) and \(\sigma_n\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(d_n>0\) and \(0\le\sigma_n\le2\) for all \(n>0\), if
\[

\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\frac{d_n}{n\log(en)}\to0,
\]
then
\[
\frac{\min\{1,\min\{u_{n,d_n},h_{n,d_n,\sigma_n}\}\}}
{h_{n,d_n,\sigma_n}}
\to0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
